package_info.package_manager: N/A (native Windows executables, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (modifies arbitrary native executables on affected systems)
package_info.why_malicious: Azov wiper is considered malicious because it injects destructive code into native Windows executables, irreversibly corrupting files and rendering systems inoperable. It masquerades as ransomware but offers no decryption or recovery mechanism, indicating its sole purpose is data destruction.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into native Windows executable files (.exe, .dll)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injected code enumerates files in target directories, overwrites executable files with random data, deletes non-executable files, and then terminates the process, resulting in irreversible data destruction.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is highly suspicious because legitimate software does not overwrite or delete large numbers of files on a system without user consent or clear purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal executables should not self-modify or corrupt other binaries; this code intentionally destroys data, violating user trust and system integrity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Secure file erasure tools may overwrite files for privacy, but only when explicitly invoked by the user and never by injecting into unrelated executables.

attack_chain.action: Initial infection: Azov wiper is delivered and executed on the victim system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code injection into native executables

attack_chain.action: Malicious payload injects code into native Windows executables.
attack_chain.leads_to: Destructive payload is present in multiple system files

attack_chain.action: When an infected executable is launched, the injected code executes, overwriting or deleting files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Irreversible data destruction and system inoperability

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected modification of native Windows executables
Mass file overwriting with random data
Deletion of user and system files without user interaction
Injected code that executes on process launch
file_indicators: Executable files with altered hashes not matching known-good versions
Presence of random data in .exe/.dll files
Sudden disappearance of user documents and executables
network_indicators: Typically none for Azov wiper (no C2 or exfiltration), but may masquerade as ransomware with fake ransom notes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to executable files, especially those with unexpected code sections or altered hashes. Alert on mass file overwriting or deletion events initiated by processes not associated with legitimate file erasure tools. Use endpoint protection to detect known Azov wiper signatures and behaviors, and monitor for the presence of injected code in system binaries.
